text:
maria: FYI customer ACME on Dedicated is seeing 429s during their morning spike. They say reserved pool should absorb bursts but we're still returning rate_limited errors. Logs attached in case thread helps. Anyone seen this behavior recently?

ashok: grabbing logs now. quick glance — the gateway is returning 429 with reason 'throughput_cap'. looks like the pool's per-second token bucket drained and refill didn't keep up. can you share pool_id and sample request rate?

maria: pool_id: pool-78f3. customer reports burst ~450 rps sustained for ~90s, then repeated 429s for next 2–3m. they expected reserved pool steady qps=300 with burst_capacity=600.

jordan: can you paste the exact 429 response body (headers+body)? need to know whether we hit global rate limiter or pool-level.

maria: pasted below: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-Redwood-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-Redwood-RateLimit-Reset: 45
{ "error": "Rate limit exceeded", "scope": "reserved_pool", "pool_id": "pool-78f3", "policy": "throughput_cap" }
```

ashok: that confirms reserved_pool scope. Possible causes: 1) inaccurate burst accounting (we count in tokens per 1s window vs customer expectation), 2) simultaneous background tasks eating capacity (prefetch/async cache warmups), 3) misconfigured pool mapping (some routes not bound to pool and draining shared capacity).

taylor: also check SLA alignment. SLA for Dedicated is based on reserved steady capacity; burst is best-effort up to configured burst_capacity but we do apply a smoothing filter to avoid instability. if their traffic pattern is long plateau (90s), the burst budget will deplete. customer might be confusing instantaneous peak with sustainable burst.

jordan: asking on customer side — can you run this repro so we can correlate? quick load script (curl loop) they can run from a single host: 
```
for i in {1..500}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" \n  -H "X-Redwood-Pool: pool-78f3" \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-base-1","input":"hello world"}' &\ndone; wait
```

samir: run with `-n` parallel workers to simulate multiple clients. also suggest adding `-H "X-Request-ID: repro-<timestamp>"` so we can find the traces. we need a sample trace id when the 429 happens.

maria: customer ran it and attached logs. 429s start at ~t+40s and continue intermittently. they say console shows pool metrics: steady_qps 300, burst_tokens 600, but dashboard shows token_count going negative during the episode.

ashok: token_count negative suggests a race between accounting and refill loop — maybe refill interval misaligned after a deploy. @deploy-bot any recent runtime patches to batching/refill?

deploy-bot: Production runtime svc:v2.14.1 rolled out 12m before customer's incident. No hotfixes scheduled.

ashok: ok that timing matches. dev-runtime team, can you confirm refill schedule (we used to refill every 250ms, we changed to 1s in v2.14.1 to reduce jitter). that could increase apparent drain during short bursts.

jordan: meanwhile for customer-facing mitigation: 1) temporarily raise steady_qps to 400 for pool-78f3 2) enable 'graceburst' mode (adds a leaky bucket over 60s) 3) route non-critical endpoints to a lower-cost variant to reduce pressure. Which is fastest?

taylor: quickest is raise steady_qps via console — takes effect within ~60s. enabling graceburst requires config change and a deploy to a policy service (short). routing endpoints needs app-side change. recommend raising steady_qps as stopgap.

maria: customer approved temporary steady_qps bump to 420. I'll apply and monitor. please keep investigating root cause.

samir: repro advice for eng: reproduce locally by running sustained 450 rps for >60s and watch token refill timing. use this helper script to simulate refill granularity: 
```
# simulate token bucket locally
BUCKET=600\nRATE=300\nREFILL_INTERVAL_MS=1000 # mimic v2.14.1\n# run generator sending at 450 rps and watch bucket
```

ashok: initial guess: the change from 250ms->1s refills increases short-term variance so bursts that used to be smoothed now deplete tokens faster; combined with per-request accounting rounding could produce negative counts. patch idea: add fractional token accounting and jittered refill to spread out refills. will prototype.

maria: customer reports fewer 429s after steady_qps bump. logging shows pool token_count staying non-negative now. good sign.

jordan: next steps for support: collect 2h of metrics post-change and confirm SLA windows (p99 latency and availability) unchanged. for eng-runtime: repro + a unit test that simulates different refill intervals and long narrow bursts. for product: clarify docs about burst semantics (sustainable vs instantaneous).

taylor: adding to backlog: PROD-6021 'refill interval-induced negative token accounting' with priority P2. include migration plan to avoid regressions during deploys.

samir: also add an automated alert: if token_count < 0 or X-Redwood-RateLimit-Remaining header spikes to 0 for a pool while pool steady_qps >= requested_sla, page oncall.

maria: thanks all — reopening if 429s reoccur. customer happy with temporary fix. assigning follow-ups: @ashok to prototyping patch, @jordan to collect metrics & close loop with customer, @taylor to update docs.

support-bot: Noted. Follow-up reminder set for 48h.

maria: marking resolved for now :thumbsup:
